settings.headline: Numbing gel, matched to the appointment.
settings.subhead: Three strengths — Clinical, Advanced and Professional — in a gel that stays where you put it. Gel is the format for precise, facial work and longer sittings where a cream would migrate. The strength you need depends on the session: how long it runs, how sensitive the area is, how demanding the work. Here's how to choose.

settings.headline: Match your numbing gel to the session
settings.body: Gel is the precise format — it holds on facial and contoured areas and stays put through a longer sitting. Within it, the strength is the choice that matters. None is "better" than another; each is formulated for a different kind of session.
settings.note: Most people don't need the top of the range. Match it to the session you're actually having — if you're between two, the lower one is usually the sensible start, and you can move up next time.

settings.label: Cream
settings.body: Broad coverage and most appointments; the default for larger or simpler areas.

settings.label: Spray
settings.body: Large or awkward-to-reach areas where applying an even layer by hand is fiddly.

settings.headline: Is gel the right format?
settings.body: Gel is the one to reach for when the work is precise or facial, or when a sitting runs long enough that a cream would start to move. Two cases where another format fits better:

settings.headline: What numbing gel is for
settings.intro: Gel suits precise, facial work and longer sittings where it needs to stay exactly where it's placed. The procedures it's most often chosen for:
settings.closer: For larger or body areas, a spray covers ground faster — and for broad, simpler areas, cream is the default. Match the format to the work.

settings.headline: Built for the procedure, not the average
settings.body: A generic numbing product treats every situation the same — the same thing for a five-minute touch-up and a full facial session. Aesthetic appointments aren't the same, so Senseless isn't built that way. The Senseless System pairs three strengths with three formats, each formulated for what a kind of appointment actually asks for. Gel exists because some work needs a format that stays exactly where it's placed. You choose by the session in front of you, not by whatever's labelled "strongest".

settings.heading: Before you buy: the bit most sellers skip
settings.body: For a lot of aesthetic procedures, the clinic applies its own numbing as standard — microneedling especially. If yours does, you may not need to bring your own, and arriving already numbed without checking can get in the way of the treatment. Self-applied numbing matters most where the practitioner doesn't provide it, or where you want extra preparation on top. A quick message to your practitioner before you book settles it.

settings.question: When should I use gel instead of cream?
settings.answer: Reach for gel when the work is precise or facial, or when a sitting runs long enough that a cream would start to move — it holds where you place it. Cream suits broad coverage and most appointments; gel suits microneedling, facial work and longer sittings.

settings.question: Which gel strength should I choose?
settings.answer: Match it to the session, not to price. Clinical for shorter, routine appointments; Advanced for longer or more sensitive work and larger areas; Professional for the most demanding sessions. If you're between two, start with the lower one.

settings.question: Is gel stronger than cream?
settings.answer: No. The three strengths — Clinical, Advanced, Professional — run across both formats. A Clinical gel matches a Clinical cream on strength; the difference is the format, not the strength. Choose gel for how it sits on the skin, not for an assumed strength difference.

settings.question: How long before my appointment do I apply numbing gel?
settings.answer: Allow time for it to take effect before your appointment, and cover the area if the window is longer — follow the product guidance and your practitioner. Customers who get on best apply a visible layer that sits on the surface rather than being rubbed in.

settings.question: Which size do I need?
settings.answer: 15ml suits a single session, a smaller area, or a trial; 35ml is the regular size for repeat use or larger areas. Both sizes are available in all three strengths.

settings.question: Do I need to patch test?
settings.answer: Yes — patch test 24 hours before on the inside of your wrist or behind your ear, and don't use it if you see any reaction. Take extra care on sensitive or broken skin.

settings.question: Is numbing gel a medicine?
settings.answer: No. Senseless is a cosmetic product, UK-formulated and CPSR assessed — no prescription needed.

settings.question: What's in it?
settings.answer: Each formula is a UK cosmetic formulated by Matrix Health Group Ltd, with the full ingredients (INCI) listed on the pack.

settings.heading: Not sure which to choose?
settings.body: Answer three quick questions — treatment, skin and session length — and we'll point you to the format and strength we'd reach for.
